parameters.text: =Workers Teleported to task location and tasks assigned.

body.buildRequest: Create three workers and have them collaboratively start building a small survival house near the leader’s current position. The house should have an approximate footprint of 7x7 to 9x9 blocks, 3-block-high walls, and a simple gable or sloped roof outline. It must become progressively enclosed and mob-safe as they work, with at minimum a complete floor and mostly complete walls by the time the initial build phase is done. Use simple, common materials such as wood planks/logs and optionally cobblestone/stone for accents.

Worker1.scope: Operate only within x:minX to x:sec1X of the rectangular footprint and full z:minZ to z:maxZ, plus the roof line and outline above this section and along the shared boundaries at x:minX and x:sec1X.
subtasks: Lightly level the ground only within your third (remove grass, flowers, and small 1-block bumps) without deep excavation or wide terrain clearing.
Lay down the floor across your third using a consistent material (e.g., oak_planks) at a single flat Y-level that all workers can match.

Build exterior walls in your third up to full height (~3 blocks), using a simple pattern (e.g., logs at corners and at x:sec1X boundary, planks in between), leaving room for 1 small window if appropriate.
Start your third of the roof outline (gable or simple slope): place the lower roof layer and establish the roof angle so Workers 2 and 3 can extend it.
Seal obvious gaps in your walls where mobs could easily enter; prioritize creating a mostly enclosed shell on your side.
Place a few exterior lights (torches/lanterns) on the outside of your wall and corner at x:minX to reduce mob spawns.
Worker1.objective: Build the western third of the house footprint (negative-X side): local ground prep and full structural shell for that third (floor, walls, roof outline).
Worker1.assumptions: Assume a roughly clear area exists near the leader for a 7x7 to 9x9 house. Workers 2 and 3 will match your floor Y-level, wall height, materials, and roof angle at the shared boundaries.
Worker1.constraints: Do NOT place or break blocks beyond x:sec1X except exactly on that boundary to connect walls and roof. Do not modify terrain or builds outside the defined footprint.
Worker1.blockBreakLimit: Only break blocks directly obstructing the footprint, walls, or roof in your third; avoid mass clearing and keep total block breaks under approximately 40 blocks.

Worker2.scope: Operate only within x:sec1X to x:sec2X of the footprint and full z:minZ to z:maxZ, plus the roof outline directly above this section and along the shared boundaries at x:sec1X and x:sec2X.
subtasks: Match Worker1’s floor level and material, extending the floor across your central third to create a continuous interior base.
Build walls in your third up to the same height and using the same style as Worker1, ensuring clean joins at x:sec1X and leaving enough solid wall for structural appearance.
Add a small, centrally placed window or two if it improves symmetry without weakening the structure.
Extend the roof outline from Worker1’s section across your third, following the same slope/angle and ensuring no gaps at the x:sec1X boundary.
Check for gaps between your walls and roof outline and close any obvious entry points that would compromise early mob safety.
Place interior lighting in your third (torches/lanterns on walls) to help keep the shared interior spawn-safe as the build progresses.
Worker2.objective: Build the central third of the house: connect left and right sections, extend the floor and walls, and continue the roof outline.
Worker2.assumptions: Assume Worker1 has defined the base palette, floor Y-level, and initial roof angle; mirror that style and pass it seamlessly toward Worker3’s section.
Worker2.constraints: Do NOT place or break blocks beyond x:sec1X or x:sec2X except exactly on those boundaries to stitch the sections together. Leave final door placement and detailed furnishing for later phases (likely to Worker3).
Worker2.blockBreakLimit: Minimize breaking; only remove blocks that obstruct continuous floor or walls in your section, staying under roughly 30 block breaks.

Worker3.scope: Operate only within x:sec2X to x:maxX of the footprint and full z:minZ to z:maxZ, plus the roof outline above this section and the shared boundary at x:sec2X. Interior work should be limited to basic floor and wall closure in your third for now.
subtasks: Extend the floor at the same Y-level and with the same material across your third, perfectly aligning with Worker2’s floor.
Build exterior walls in your third with the same pattern and height as the other sections, adding 1 small window if appropriate while keeping enough solid wall for future door placement.
Continue the roof outline from Worker2’s boundary at x:sec2X and bring it to a clean end at x:maxX, matching the existing slope and style.
Ensure your walls and roof outline leave the structure mostly enclosed on your side, with minimal open gaps.
Reserve a suitable wall section (often along a long side or at the positive-X short side) where a main entrance door can later be added without major redesign.
Add a bit of interior and exterior lighting in your third, focusing on closing off dark corners near your walls.
Worker3.objective: Build the eastern third of the house (positive-X side), extending the floor, walls, and roof outline, and prepare space for future entrance and interior details.
Worker3.assumptions: Assume Workers 1 and 2 have already established a consistent palette, wall height, and roof angle to be mirrored. Assume that once doors, full roof blocks, and furniture are added in a later step, the house will become fully mob-safe and functional.
Worker3.constraints: Do NOT build outside x:sec2X to x:maxX, except exactly on x:sec2X where you connect walls and roof to Worker2’s section. Avoid large-scale terrain reshaping or modifying any nearby structures.
Worker3.blockBreakLimit: Limit breaking to what is needed to align floor/walls and remove minor obstructions; keep total breaks under approximately 40 blocks.
